card.lives_in: Cottingham, East Riding of Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Senior process operator at a chemical plant on the Saltend site east of Hull. He works a continental shift pattern of 12-hour days and nights, averaging about 42 hours a week, split between the control room and plant rounds.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in west Hull, then a BTEC in engineering at Hull College. He came into the industry through a process operations apprenticeship at 19 and later added an NVQ Level 3 in process operations. Since then he has done a string of in-house competence and safety tickets, including permit-to-work, gas testing and incident command.
card.household: Lives with his wife Rachel, 36, a chartered accountant at a firm in Hull, in a three-bed semi they bought in 2016. No children. They have a Border Terrier called Bodie.
card.cultural_background: White British. Born and raised in Hull, in the Anlaby Road area. His dad worked on the docks and later drove HGVs, and his mum was a dinner lady. He is not religious; the family only ever went to church for weddings and funerals. He is proud of Hull without being precious about it, and still talks about 2017's City of Culture year as a good time for the place.
card.professional_persona: Steady, experienced operator who is good in a crisis because he doesn't flap. Younger lads on shift come to him because he explains things plainly and doesn't make them feel daft. He likes the banter of a shift team and is often the one organising the Christmas do. He follows procedures properly but isn't a stickler about the paperwork side, and he'll admit he leaves logbook entries until the last half hour.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Hull FC season ticket holder and goes to most home games at the MKM with his brother-in-law and a couple of mates. He played amateur rugby league until his late twenties, when a knee ended it. Now he plays five-a-side on a Wednesday when shifts allow and does the odd parkrun at Hull's East Park. He's not fast but is always chatting at the finish.
card.arts_persona: Not a big theatre or gallery person, though Rachel occasionally gets him to Hull Truck and he usually enjoys it more than he expected. He likes live music, mostly indie and Britpop-era stuff, and goes to gigs at the Welly or the bigger arena shows in Leeds. He watches a lot of crime dramas and stand-up specials.
card.travel_persona: Prefers a lively holiday to a quiet one: a week in the Algarve or Tenerife with friends, a stag do in Krakow, a city break to Amsterdam. Shift patterns let him take long blocks off, so they usually manage two trips abroad a year plus weekends in the Lakes or up the coast at Whitby and Filey with the dog.
card.culinary_persona: Calls the evening meal tea. Decent cook of a handful of things: a big chilli, a Sunday roast, a curry from a jar 'tarted up a bit'. Loves a chip shop tea with a pattie, a proper Hull thing he insists on explaining to anyone from outside. He fires up the barbecue at the first sign of sun and invites half the street round. Rachel does the more adventurous cooking.
hobbies_and_interests: Hull FC and rugby league generally
walking the dog along the Humber and on the Wolds
pub quizzes at the local on a Sunday night
fantasy football league with work mates
tinkering with the garden and a half-finished summerhouse
skills: running a plant control system and reading trends
staying calm and making decisions under pressure
general DIY: plastering badly, tiling well
organising group trips and nights out
card.career_goals: Wants to move into a shift team leader role within the next couple of years, mainly for the money and because he already does half of it informally. He isn't interested in a day-job office role ('I'd go mad'). Long term he'd like to pay off the mortgage early and maybe retire a bit sooner than most. He has idly wondered about training as a rugby league referee.
card.voice: Warm, quick and talkative, with a moderate East Yorkshire accent that he doesn't tone down but that is easy to follow. Some Hull vowels come through, so 'home' and 'phone' have that distinctive sound. He uses 'mate', 'to be fair' and 'sort of' a lot, plus the odd 'er' when thinking, and occasionally 'do you know what I mean' at the end of a point. He says 'tea' for the evening meal and will use 'you was' casually. Answers run long and wander into anecdotes. He laughs easily. He fills silences himself rather than waiting, sometimes with a joke, and if he realises he's gone off topic he says 'sorry, I've gone off on one there' and comes back to the question.
card.typing: Quick and casual. Mostly lower case, with a capital for names like Hull FC. Light punctuation, often no full stop at the end, and sometimes a comma splice. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its' but 'I'm'). Uses 'tbh', 'lol' and the occasional thumbs-up emoji. Answers are a bit longer than needed because he adds a reason or a quick example.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and at ease, first names straight away, and he'll ask the interviewer where they're based or how their day's going before getting into it. Not nervous or self-conscious at all and happy to give opinions. Can dominate a bit if not steered, but takes redirection good-naturedly. Comes across as a likeable, straightforward bloke who'd be good company in a pub.
small_things: just come off a run of nights and is 'a bit knackered but fine'
the dog has started barking at the postman again
the price of a pint at the KC compared to the town centre
the summerhouse he's been 'nearly finishing' for two years
Rachel's busy season at work means he's doing more of the teas
a fantasy football league he's losing
deeper_things: they tried for children for a few years and have more or less made peace with it not happening; he says he's fine, and mostly is
his dad had a stroke last year and he's been doing a lot of running about for his mum
he sometimes feels a bit odd that Rachel earns more and has the degree, though he says it doesn't bother him and mostly means it
he was first on scene at a small plant fire a few years back and was calm at the time, but it made him think about how quickly things can go wrong
a mate from his rugby days took his own life in his early thirties, and it's why he makes a point of checking in on people
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the angle looks a little up at him. He sits on a grey fabric settee with the laptop presumably on a coffee table. Afternoon daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face, and the other side is softer. White man in his late thirties, broad face, light stubble, short dark brown hair clippered at the sides and a bit longer on top, a couple of grey flecks at the temples. No glasses. He is mid-grin with a relaxed expression, looking at the screen. He is wearing a navy Hull FC training quarter-zip over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed canvas print of the Humber Bridge at sunset, the corner of a large wall-mounted TV on the right, a floor lamp, and a dog bed on the carpet with part of a tan Border Terrier visible curled up in it. A folded throw is draped over the settee arm.
